caption:

author: Upendra Singh Rathore  • 2nd
caption:
🤔 Should you pursue M.Tech from DTU?
As an M.Tech alumnus of DTU, one question I frequently receive from students is:
"Is M.Tech from DTU worth it?"
My answer is: It depends on what you're expecting from it.
 Go for M.Tech at DTU if:
• You want to build strong technical expertise in your domain.
• You are interested in research, higher studies, or specialized engineering roles.
• You want to study in a reputed institution with a strong alumni network.
• You are willing to take advantage of projects, faculty mentorship, and industry exposure.
 Think twice if:
• You're pursuing M.Tech only because you couldn't decide what to do after B.Tech.
• You're expecting the degree itself to guarantee a high-paying job.
• You're not willing to invest time in skill development, networking, and practical learning.
One thing I've learned is that DTU provides a solid platform, but your growth depends on how you utilize the opportunities available.
Many students compare M.Tech with taking up a job immediately after B.Tech. There is no universally correct answer.
➡️ If your priority is earning as soon as possible, a job may be the better choice.
➡️ If your goal is specialization, advanced technical knowledge, research exposure, or long-term career growth, M.Tech can be a worthwhile investment.
My conclusion:
M.Tech from DTU is not a shortcut to success, nor is it a waste of time. It is an opportunity. For students with clear goals and the willingness to put in the effort, it can be one of the most rewarding decisions of their professional journey.
#DTU #MTech #DelhiTechnologicalUniversity #Engineering #HigherEducation #CareerGrowth #GATE #Technology #Learning

author: Parikh Jain Premium Profile FollowingParikh Jain  • FollowingFounder @ ProPeers | Ex-Amazon | Ex-Founding Member at Coding Ninjas | Youtuber(80k+) | DTU
caption:
A child who scores less than others gets called dumb.

An adult who earns less than others gets called useless.

That is how casually we hurt people in this society.

We look at one job title, salary slip, exam result, and then we act like we have understood a whole human being. 

We judge fast, label faster, and move on without thinking what those words do to someone’s mind over years.

Take this example.

One son works in IT, earns ₹45 lakh a year, and sends money home every month.

The other son lives in the village, owns 8 acres of farmland, earns less, and people call him useless.

Useless according to whom? What do they know about him?

The saddest part is not just the comparison, it's also how early it starts.

A child grows up hearing he is behind.
An adult grows up hearing he is not enough.

And after a point, people do not even need society to insult them anymore. 

They start doing it to themselves.

We need to stop calling people useless just because their life does not fit the one template we respect.

A person can score less and still become wise, kind, capable, and strong.
A person can choose a different road and still build the life of their dreams. 

Not everyone who looks smaller from the outside is living a smaller life.
Sometimes the only thing that is small is the way we judge them.

author: Rignor Labs
caption:
AI Engineer is no longer a single role.

One AI Engineer builds products with LLMs using RAG, agents, APIs, and system design.

Another AI Engineer builds the models themselves through architecture design, training, optimization, and research.

Same title.
Different skills.
Different interviews.
Different career paths.

Know which one you’re preparing for.

#AIEngineer #ArtificialIntelligence #GenerativeAI #LLM #MachineLearning #AIAgents #PromptEngineering #RAG #MCP #SystemDesign #LLMOps #MLOps #AIProducts #AIResearch #DeepLearning #TechCareers #SoftwareEngineering #DataScience #OpenAI #FutureOfWork
